account:
So far today I have not found solid evidence of unusual activity, despite my feeling that something may be happening without my knowledge. During my morning market walk, Townsfolk 10, 20 and 30 each said they had no news. The secretary reported no correspondence or unusual news and offered to receive concerns while I was out. She has my appointment book for safekeeping; I saw her take it from the office chest. That fits her duties, rather than indicating anything secret.

The builder repeatedly asked me to specify repair work and payment. I asked for an inspection and priced report at my office at thirteen, without authorizing work. This seems to be unresolved town business, not evidence of a hidden scheme. I should clarify it when we meet.

The innkeeper eventually answered my questions: eight fresh loaves for meals, no lodging requests, no town concerns, and plans to check accommodation and clear spoiled stock. The secretary has offered to relay guest or catering needs. That sounds like ordinary inn business. The baker also advertised fresh bread at one emerald a loaf. I heard some distant conversation I could not understand; I cannot infer its subject.

I am home after keeping my noon lunch engagement. Next are office accounts and the requested builder report at thirteen, tea at the dockside cottage at fifteen, and the office at sixteen-thirty. For now, there is no identified unusual undertaking, no established group involved, and no supported explanation for my unease. I should keep my appointments and continue asking discreet, factual questions rather than treating routine dealings as suspicious.
